issues.description: Missing/relocated global framebuffer symbol 'display_start': the problem statement and the template declare and refer to a global symbol named 'display_start' as the framebuffer base address, but the solution file still references the same identifier (in set_pixel and in main) while not providing a corresponding global declaration. This mismatch (code uses the symbol but there is no global definition in the solution) will cause assembly/linker errors and confuses students about where the framebuffer buffer is defined and how to match the template description.
issues.suggestedFix: Restore a consistent, accessible declaration of 'display_start' or adapt the code and documentation to the chosen design. Two acceptable fixes: (A) Reintroduce a global buffer declaration (e.g. in .bss: 'display_start RESB 8294400') so both main and set_pixel can reference it as in the template and problem statement; or (B) keep an explicitly local framebuffer (allocated in main) but then modify all references and calls so the address is passed to set_pixel (e.g. pass pointer in a register or on the stack) and update the problem statement/template to document the differing design. Ensure the symbol name used in code matches where the buffer is declared and that the final repository compiles without undefined-symbol errors.
